_generated_by: AI-generated with Claude Code (Anthropic), directed and reviewed by the Moonat team.
interpolation: cubic Hermite (C1) on positions; slerp on quaternion
interpolation_scheme: Record k of <Y>.bin is at POSIX time T(Y)+k*H*3600 s (T(Y) = Y-01-01T00:00:00Z; POSIX ignores leap seconds, like JS Date). For time t in year Y: u=(t-T(Y))/(H*3600), i=min(floor(u),N-2), s=u-i. Positions (sun_me, earth_me, planets_icrs; per component) use cubic Hermite with per-step tangents m_k=(P[k+1]-P[k-1])/2 for 1<=k<=N-2, m_0=(-11P[0]+18P[1]-9P[2]+2P[3])/6, m_(N-1)=(11P[N-1]-18P[N-2]+9P[N-3]-2P[N-4])/6; P(s)=(2s^3-3s^2+1)P[i]+(s^3-2s^2+s)m_i+(-2s^3+3s^2)P[i+1]+(s^3-s^2)m_(i+1). Planet directions are renormalised. Quaternion: slerp from q[i] to q[i+1] after negating q[i+1] if dot(q[i],q[i+1])<0. Rotation matrix from (w,x,y,z): Hamilton, active, v_me = R v_icrs. Topocentric: site_me = (1737.4 + (ground_elev_m+observer_height_m)/1000) km * (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat); body_topo = body_me - site_me; planets have no parallax (unit vectors). Reference: moonat.ephem.table (Python).
quaternion: q_icrs_to_me = (w, x, y, z), Hamilton, active: v_me = q v_icrs q*
apparent: seen from the Moon's centre: light-time + gravitational deflection (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn) + stellar aberration; vector length = light-time distance (km)
planet_note: jupiter and saturn are system barycentres (DE421); offset < 0.1 arcsec
interp_error_note: Max over random times and the first/last interval of every year, table vs direct skyfield, Moon-centre vectors. Includes the intervals holding a leap second (POSIX time cannot represent 23:59:60, so up to 1 s of lunar rotation, ~0.55 arcsec, there). Elsewhere the Sun error is <= 0.1 arcsec at a 3 h step.
